subject: Defining acceptance gates, test artifacts & MAP for Novamed evaluation
messages:
From: Jenna Cole <jenna.cole@novamed.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation acceptance criteria & MAP — initial ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. Procurement asked that we formalize the evaluation acceptance criteria so legal and engineering can sign off before we kick off the 6-week pilot.

What we need from Redwood: a short mutual action plan (MAP) with concrete exit gates (pass/fail), a catalog of acceptance tests (smoke + functional), and a short list of evidence artifacts we can attach to our procurement package (sample logs, test scripts, security questionnaires). Can you share a draft by Friday so I can circulate?

Key constraints for us:
- Clinical data pseudonymization must be validated in the trial environment
- 99% inference availability during business hours (M-F 8am–6pm PT) for the evaluation window
- Example dataset (10k records) processing with <350ms p95 per request

If helpful, I can share a template of what procurement expects.

Thanks,
Jenna Cole
Head of Data Science, Novamed Health
[Attachment: Novamed-procurement-template.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jenna Cole <jenna.cole@novamed.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance criteria & MAP — initial ask

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear ask.

We can absolutely put a short MAP together that maps the evaluation timeline to unambiguous acceptance gates. I'll draft a compact MAP that includes:
- 6-week evaluation timeline with milestones and owners
- 5 concrete exit gates (data handling, latency, availability, quality/QA, security evidence)
- Acceptance test catalog (smoke tests + 6 functional checks) with pass criteria and sample commands/data
- Evidence artifacts (sample sanitized logs, KV-cache snapshots, system metrics export)

Lauren (CS) and Marissa (SE) are looped in to define test owners and access needs. Proposed delivery: draft MAP + test catalog by EOD Friday (2025-05-23). Is that okay for you?

Action items from our side:
1) Karthik — owner for MAP and high-level acceptance wording
2) Marissa — build test scripts and sample dataset (anonymized)
3) Lauren — coordinate trial access and SSO/provisioning with Novamed IT

We will include a short evidence log template you can paste into procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Novamed-MAP-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Jenna Cole <jenna.cole@novamed.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance criteria & MAP — initial ask

Hi Jenna — quick technical note and proposed test cases.

Technical assumptions for acceptance tests:
- Trial environment will run on Dedicated sandbox in us-west-2 (non-prod network with pseudonymized dataset)
- We'll provide an S3 bucket with sample files and a short ingest script (see test-catalog).
- For availability checks we'll run a synthetic 1qps load with 95th percentile latency measured over 30m windows.

Proposed minimal acceptance test catalog (summarized):
1) Smoke: single request success, correct output schema (JSON keys match contract)
2) Latency: p95 < 350ms over 30m window on provided 10k sample (pass/fail)
3) Throughput: sustained 10 qps for 10m without error rate >1%
4) Data handling: no unmasked PHI elements in sanitized samples (tooling we provide will verify)
5) Quality: top-1 label accuracy >= 92% on labeled sample set (excerpt included)
6) Failover: routing to fallback model within 200ms when primary node unavailable

I attached the initial acceptance-test-catalog and a tiny log sample for evidence formatting. If procurement needs specific schema names I can align.

marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acceptance-test-catalog.md (markdown)]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Jenna Cole <jenna.cole@novamed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance criteria & MAP — initial ask

Hi Jenna — quick ops notes so the trial can be scheduled once tests are agreed:

Provisioning checklist:
- SSO / SAML connector and test user created (we'll need an admin contact)
- VPC peering or private link set-up for sample dataset transfer (security approval)
- Service account with read-only access to the evidence S3 bucket for our metrics exporter

Evidence log template (paste into procurement):
- Test name, date/time, owner, raw artifact path (s3://...), pass/fail, notes, link to test run summary (Drive)

Suggested go/no-go exit gates (short form):
- Data gate: sanitized dataset verification complete and tooling report attached
- Latency gate: p95 < 350ms for 3 consecutive 30m windows during business hours
- Availability gate: >= 99% uptime measured by exporter across evaluation window
- Quality gate: model accuracy >= 92% on labeled holdout
- Security gate: completed security questionnaire + AWS account audit snapshot attached

If these look good we can convert into a short MAP doc and share DocuSign-ready language for procurement.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: log-sample-s3.txt (text)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jenna Cole <jenna.cole@novamed.com>, procurement@novamed.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance criteria & MAP — draft delivered

Jenna / Novamed procurement — attaching the draft MAP and acceptance test catalog per our plan. Highlights below and proposed next steps.

Summary highlights (from attached MAP):
- 6-week evaluation start window: target start 2025-06-02 (owner: Novamed IT for provisioning)
- Milestone week 1: provisioning + sample dataset ingest
- Milestone week 2–4: run functional and quality tests; weekly syncs
- Milestone week 5: ramped availability/throughput testing
- Milestone week 6: final evidence package and signoff

Proposed acceptance gates (pass/fail):
- Data gate: pass if sanitizer report shows zero unmasked PHI fields on submitted sample (artifact: sanitizer-report.json)
- Latency gate: pass if p95 < 350ms for three business-hour windows
- Availability gate: pass if uptime >= 99% as measured by our exporter
- Quality gate: pass if labeled-holdout accuracy >= 92%
- Security gate: pass if questionnaire and AWS audit snapshot included

Next steps:
- Jenna: confirm the proposed start date and provide Novamed admin contact for SSO
- Procurement: confirm whether the attached MAP language is sufficient for contract exhibit; we can prep DocuSign clause if needed
- Novamed IT: we will send an infra checklist and provisioning playbook once admin contact is listed

Attachments (in email): Novamed-MAP-draft.xlsx, acceptance-test-catalog.md, log-sample-s3.txt

Thanks — we'll stand up a short kickoff call once you confirm.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://drive.google.com/novamed/MAP-draft]
